subject: Provisional availability waiver + monthly credit reconciliation plan
messages:
From: Kim Alvarez <kim@cloudwave.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudWave Procurement <procurement@cloudwave.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: short-term availability waiver during migration (Nov)

Hi Nikhil,

We’re running a staged migration of our user traffic to the new routing fabric the week of Nov 15. The migration plan has a non-trivial toggle window where a small percentage of traffic will be routed to a blue cluster while we validate infra — that raises the risk of false-positive availability blips during the window.

Can Redwood provide a provisional availability waiver for the migration window (Nov 15–22) to avoid triggering standard monthly credits for transient, expected degradations?

What we’re proposing from our side:
- Keep the standard monitoring enabled and share alerts/logs in real time.
- Define an explicit list of maintenance-like events that will be excluded (traffic switch, reindex job, db migration) and provide timelines in advance.
- Agree a reconciliation approach that limits monthly credits to either a fixed cap (e.g., $40k) or X% of the invoice for Nov.

Attached is our migration runbook for context. We’d like to get this locked before Nov 8 if possible — procurement is on a tight timeline for sign-off.

Attachments: CloudWave-migration-plan.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Kim Alvarez
Head of Cloud Platform — CloudWave
kim@cloudwave.com
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
To: Kim Alvarez <kim@cloudwave.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term availability waiver during migration (Nov)

Kim — thanks for the runbook, that helps.

High level response: we can support a provisional waiver but need a narrowly-scoped amendment to the standard SLA that: (a) defines exact timeboxes, (b) enumerates excluded event types, (c) caps the total monthly credit exposure for the invoice period, and (d) sets measurement windows and post-migration reconciliation steps.

I’ve drafted a short amendment (attached) that implements a tiered reconciliation: a temporary baseline availability of 99.0% for the waiver window, with credits limited to the lesser of 10% of November invoice or $40,000; any availability shortfall outside the enumerated migration events will be handled per standard SLA.

Next steps I suggest:
- Internal review from Laura / Marissa on the legal/finance side (cc’d).
- If that looks OK, we’ll send a redline to your procurement and then prepare the DocuSign envelope.
- We’ll also agree monitoring hooks — we can provide a read-only dashboard and export logs for the migration window.

Attached: provisional-waiver-draft.docx (docx)

I’ll wait on Laura / Marissa for final signal before sending to procurement.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
nikhil@redwood.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kim Alvarez <kim@cloudwave.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T10:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term availability waiver during migration (Nov)

Nikhil / Kim — I reviewed the draft and left a few clarifying edits. Key points from legal/finance:

1) Baseline and cap
- Our standard hosted availability baseline is 99.95% (monthly). For a short-term, limited waiver we’re amenable to a provisional baseline of 99.0% for the calendar window Nov 15–22 only.
- Credits for the waiver window will be capped at the lesser of: (a) 10% of the November invoice, or (b) $40,000. This cap is intended to limit one-off exposure while still providing recourse.

2) Exclusions and fencing
- Excluded events must be scheduled and notified at least 48 hours in advance. Unscheduled degradations that occur during the window will be assessed — if they correlate to Redwood platform incidents (rather than CloudWave toggling), they are not excluded.

3) Measurement and reconciliation
- Measurements will be computed using Redwood’s standard measuring window (00:00–23:59 PT) and the usual availability calculation.
- Post-window reconciliation: Redwood will provide a certificate of availability and raw aggregated logs within 7 business days; CloudWave may raise disputes within 10 business days.

4) Alternate option (if CloudWave prefers)
- Instead of an availability baseline change, we can offer a temporary relaxation of the p95 latency SLO for one week with identical credit caps. That might preserve availability accounting and be operationally simpler.

If CloudWave confirms the preferred approach (availability baseline vs latency relaxation) we’ll issue a redline and route for DocuSign. I’ve added links to the HubSpot deal and a draft DocuSign envelope for convenience.

HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deals/CW-2026-0421
Draft doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/s/drive/SLA-amendment-draft
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/instance/embedded?envelopeId=abc123-or-similar

Laura Bennett
VP, Legal & Revenue Ops — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
From: Kim Alvarez <kim@cloudwave.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudWave Procurement <procurement@cloudwave.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term availability waiver during migration (Nov)

Thanks Laura — that framework looks reasonable and aligns with internal risk tolerance. Two quick asks from procurement/security:

- We’ll need read-only access to the aggregated availability dashboard and a daily export of the availability summary for the waiver window (csv).
- We’re also requesting a short SOC2 evidence bundle and a list of logging/export endpoints so our security team can validate that incidents will be detectable. I attached a small evidence checklist to this thread.

If you’re OK with those two items I’ll ask procurement to sign the redline as soon as it’s circulated.

Attachments: SOC2-evidence-request.xlsx (xlsx)

Best,
Kim
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kim Alvarez <kim@cloudwave.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T16:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term availability waiver during migration (Nov)

Looping in quick ops notes to make implementation smoother:

- Measurement windows: we’ll compute availability using PT midnight-to-midnight buckets and publish a per-day CSV by 10:00 PT the next day for the waiver period.
- Dashboard access: we’ll provision a read-only link scoped to the CloudWave account and add a webhook export to push daily aggregates to the CloudWave S3 bucket if they provide an ingress endpoint.
- Incident triage: any outage claimed as outside the enumerated migration events will trigger our normal RCA process; if CloudWave opens a dispute we’ll freeze the credit calculation for that period while we investigate.

Action items:
1) Nikhil / Laura — finalize the redline and send to Kim’s procurement ASAP.
2) Marissa — please confirm finance OK with the 10% / $40k cap and prepare the DocuSign template.
3) Ops (cc’d) — ready the dashboard export and webhook (I’ll kick off provisioning once procurement confirms the S3 target).

-Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Platform Operations — Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
